rootCauseHypothesis.evidence: Attempts 3–7 changed release intent and vertical velocity but never stored the x/y/angle/support-relative state that baseline anchored follow preserves; fixed replay failures moved through top exit, early termination, and lift-plank stall.
rootCauseHypothesis.changeHypothesis: On the exact early separating runway top-tip contact, keep status airborne and continue normal motion, but store a bounded virtual support-release pose: supportId, anchorOffsetX/Y, contact player x/y/angle. The next normal tap consumes the intent exactly once, resolves the current support transform plus stored offsets, and launches from that pose using standard support-release velocity; cancel the intent on reset/loadLevel/expiry/terminal/non-runway contact or if the support is inactive.
rootCauseHypothesis.lifecycleSemantics: remain visibly airborne while retaining a virtual support-release pose; consume exactly once by launching from the stored pose and current support transform
rejectedAlternatives: Approach-only relative-normal guard does not address the natural separating branch.

acceptanceCriteria: A RED test proves the exact upward/separating natural-pose contact anchors under the restored baseline.

The candidate records all six virtual-pose fields at the exact contact branch and clears them on reset/loadLevel/expiry/terminal/non-runway contact or inactive support.
The next normal tap consumes the intent exactly once and launches from the current support transform plus stored offsets.
The first and second deterministic runway release poses match baseline x/y/angle within a documented epsilon before velocity is applied.
Launch velocity, angular velocity, cooldown reset, input-buffer clearing, and launch event remain standard anchored-release semantics.
The pending pose does not freeze or teleport the visible player before the tap; any tap-time correction is measured and accepted by a focused test.
Non-runway support anchors and release taps remain unchanged; side sharp, approaching top, later runway suppression, and blunt bounce remain intact.
The same seed-31 fixed timestamp replay reaches at least 11.9 seconds and x>2000 without failure or authored-support stall.
Only game-core.ts and level1-recovery.test.ts change; no renderer, level, debug, platform, or shared factory files.
